# A new e2e spec plans at the median until a rebuild, so its shard overruns

## Context

#21287's post-merge AC missed on 19 Nov ([measurements](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21287#issuecomment-7014168066)): engine shard steps stopped at the five-minute ceiling with every test passed on #21450 (shards 3 and 7), #21479 (shard 14) and twice on #21468 (shard 3, runs `44546652891` and `44550608816`, "78 passed (5.1m)" both times). Vega and Ada each filed defect notes on the same symptom the same day. Ada owns the line (#21259 → #21287 → #21288) and handed this successor over (A2A `c251f8a7`, 19 Nov 16:12Z): "file the successor and do both".

## The Problem

`buildScripts/util/e2eEngineDurations.json` was rebuilt on 18 Nov (#21288). Since then 17 spec files joined the engine tier, and `durationOf()` plans each at the table's median, 9.2 s.

Measured from the 7 completed full runs of today's `dev` pushes (`44548103478`, `44534326302`, `44523126394`, `44521127253`, `44512489797`, `44505309963`, `44502234457`):

| Observation | Value |
|---|---|
| Tier files / files the table lacks | 243 / 17 |
| The 17, measured | 2.0–36.4 s each, 11 of them above the 9.2 s median (`board/SwimlanesNL` 36.4, `grid/ServerSidePagingNL` 26.8, `webdesktop/Apps` 25.1, `gantt/BigDataNL` 23.4, `colors/BackendFallback` 19.0, …) |
| Today's split, as the table plans it | 255–256 s per shard |
| The same split, priced by the 7 runs | 211–313 s per shard; shard 3, holding `colors/BackendFallback` and `webdesktop/Apps`, is the 313 s one |
| A split from a table rebuilt on the 7 runs | 254–255 s per shard |

A rebuild fixes today's 17. It decays again as the Engine 14 examples keep adding specs: #21492 adds `e2e/form/FormApp.spec.mjs` to the tier now, and it plans at the median until the next rebuild.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: "A shard nearing it gets a sibling, never a higher ceiling: the ceiling is the wait every pull request pays." (`.github/workflows/test-e2e.yml` header, *Time*)

- `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`: `durationOf(durations)` returns `durations[path] ?? median`; `balancedShard()` places files longest-first by those seconds; `ENGINE_DURATIONS`'s JSDoc says a missing file "counts as its median".
- `engineDurations(...runs)` (#21288) keeps each file's costliest run across several runs' logs; `--engine-durations` takes one log file per run.
- `FULL_SHARDS = {engine: 15}`. The 7 runs' shards averaged about 3.8 min (2.8–5.1 min on `44550608816`): the mean load fits 15 shards, so the first fix is the plan. Some files vary more than any table holds: on the PR's own run, `portal/DocsClassRoutes` cost 72.9 s against a planned 34.8 s, and its shard stopped at the ceiling. The margin for that variance is a sibling shard.

## The Fix

1. Rebuild `e2eEngineDurations.json` with `engineDurations` from the 7 runs above, so all 243 tier files carry a measured cost.
2. `durationOf()` plans a file the table lacks at the table's 90th percentile instead of its median, and the JSDoc of `durationOf` and `ENGINE_DURATIONS` say so. On today's table that is 41.3 s, above all 17 files' measured costs. An over-plan leaves its own shard light and adds about its excess divided by 15 to each other shard, while an under-plan puts the whole error on one shard, which is the shard that stops at the ceiling.

3. **Considered and declined, 19 Nov: a sixteenth shard.** On the fresh table the PR's own run (`44565270009`) stopped shard 13 at the ceiling, 57 of 57 passed. A held-out back-test puts the slowest shard at 223–240 s on 16 shards against 232–299 s on 15. The operator's runner budget decides it: 20 slots across the org, while a full Engine PR push already starts about 36 jobs. A sibling shard is one more runner on every full run. Fifteen shards cost about one shard re-run in eight runs. The overrun came from two portal docs specs at twice their seven-run maximum, which is a fix at their source.
4. **The step ceiling goes from five to six minutes** (`.github/workflows/test-e2e.yml`, the header's *Time* rule and the step's `timeout-minutes`). Ada wrote the rule (#18896) and proposed the change on 19 Nov. A stop at the ceiling costs a re-run slot, the author's repair turn and about half an hour of review delay (#21485 and #21486 that afternoon). A six-minute ceiling costs no slot. On the back-test it stops 0 of 8 runs instead of 1. The rule now reads: a shard nearing the ceiling gets its slow spec fixed first, and a sibling only when the runner budget has room.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `e2eEngineDurations.json` holds a measured time for every `enginePaths()` file, rebuilt from at least 5 full runs on today's `dev`, and the PR names their run ids.
- [ ] AC-2: A file the table lacks plans at the table's 90th percentile; `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/E2eCiSelection.spec.mjs` pins it, red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3: The PR states each shard's planned seconds with the old table and the new one, and the old split's cost under the new measurements.
- [ ] AC-5: the engine e2e step ceiling is six minutes, and the workflow header's *Time* rule names the slow spec first and a sibling only within the runner budget.
- [ ] AC-4 (post-merge): over the first 20 pull-request runs that run engine shards on a head containing the merge, no engine shard step stops at the ceiling with its tests passing, and the slowest green-head step is at most 285 s. Method as in [#21287's AC-4 window](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21287#issuecomment-6964459935). If a green-head step still passes 285 s, the first lever is the spec that overran; another shard costs a runner on every full run, and a higher ceiling is not a lever.

## Out of Scope

- A table that refreshes itself on a schedule (still out, as in #21259 and #21287): the p90 fallback makes a stale table fail safe instead.
- `FULL_SHARDS.engine`: a sixteenth shard was tried and declined on the runner budget (Fix item 3).
- `portal/ExamplesCatalogNL.spec.mjs`'s run-to-run variance (#21287's own out-of-scope item).
- The `e2e-brain` tier's table.

## Avoided Traps

- **The table's maximum as the fallback.** It is 167 s on today's table. One new file planned at 167 s pushes its excess, about 10 s, onto each of the other shards, for every file the table lacks.
- **The median.** Measured: 11 of the 17 files cost more than it, and the shard that drew two of them ran past the ceiling.
- **A sixteenth shard instead of the plan fix.** Another runner per pull request does not fix a mispriced file, so the table and the p90 fallback come first, and the variance a table cannot hold goes back to its source (Fix item 3).
- **A table from many more runs.** Built from the 30 full runs before the held-out eight, the table plans 4,297 s instead of 3,824 s, and its slowest held-out shard is 270 s with 16 shards. Per-file maxima from older spec versions unbalance the split on current runs.
